content:
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL & Data Automation

Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFILE
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design and test and validation of automotive and industrial components. Uses Python and MATLAB to process test-rig data, automate validation and reporting, and support engineering decisions. Experienced querying SQL Server test-results data for trend analysis. Interested in moving into data engineering.

EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components
Seat structures and seat-adjuster mechanisms | Setúbal | Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and conduct durability, vibration and climatic tests across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare test reports for OEM customers.
- Developed Python tools using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to process rig output files, check every channel against test specifications and generate standard report figures. Reduced report preparation time from about three days to half a day per test.
- Query the plant's SQL Server test-results database to analyse trends across three product generations.
- Correlate rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis of field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive used to select rig load profiles.

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps
Industrial centrifugal pumps | Porto | Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and produced production drawings with GD&T; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Conducted structural FEA of casings in ANSYS. Supported a change from grey cast iron to ductile iron for one casing family, saving 12% in material cost.
- Supported conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup using Siemens S7.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

SKILLS
Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib), SQL (SQL Server), MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving, Excel/VBA, Power BI

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native), English (fluent), Spanish (good)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally written, and easy to scan. It includes strong quantified achievements, especially reducing report preparation time from approximately three days to half a day and reducing warranty returns by 40%. The career history is coherent and the technical evidence is credible for a test and validation engineer moving toward data engineering. The main content limitation is not poor writing but limited evidence of data-platform engineering: the document presents data processing, database querying, and automation rather than production platforms, cloud warehouses, data modelling, orchestration, governance, or large-scale data operations.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text formatting, and recognizable technology names, so it should parse reliably in ATS systems. Python, SQL Server, MATLAB, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Power BI, and English/Portuguese are searchable keywords. ATS alignment for this particular role is nevertheless limited because the CV does not truthfully show several central terms from the advertisement, including data platform, cloud data warehouse, Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD, Git, dimensional modelling, data governance, access policies, and query optimisation on large datasets. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than document defects, so they should not be added without supporting evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible adjacent profile rather than a strong direct match for Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform. Transferable evidence includes Python automation, structured processing of test-rig data, SQL Server trend analysis, reporting automation, data validation against specifications, and measurable process improvement. Professional English and Portuguese are clearly shown, satisfying those requirements. The candidate's material does not show experience designing, building, or operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale; advanced Python and SQL with query optimisation on large datasets; dimensional data modelling; Google Cloud or a comparable cloud; graph modelling; or curiosity about open-source data architecture practices. The CV also does not demonstrate ownership of shared platforms, collaboration with analytics or data science teams, governance, access policies, or reusable data-platform frameworks. The strongest truthful positioning is as a mechanical/test engineer with substantial engineering-data automation experience transitioning toward data engineering, not as an already-qualified senior data-platform engineer.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the headline, retain the truthful focus on engineering-data automation but make the target clearer by changing "Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL & Data Automation" to "Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL & Engineering Data Automation". This better reflects the documented experience and avoids implying production data-platform experience.
2. In the Profile section, replace the final sentence "Interested in moving into data engineering." with a more specific, evidence-based transition statement such as: "Targeting data engineering roles that build on experience automating engineering-data processing and reporting with Python and analysing SQL Server test-results data." This uses the job-relevant concepts the candidate can substantiate without claiming cloud or platform experience.
3. In the Skills section, reorganize the single keyword list into ATS-friendly subgroups while preserving only documented skills. For example: "Data & Automation: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib), SQL Server, Excel/VBA, Power BI"; "Engineering & Analysis: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW, Minitab"; "Methods: DOE, GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving." This gives Python and SQL Server greater prominence for the target role and improves scanability.
4. In the current Corvane Automotive Components entry, revise the SQL bullet to include the exact database context and analytical purpose in one ATS-friendly sentence: "Queried the plant's SQL Server test-results database to analyse trends across three product generations." The current wording is already accurate; this change simply makes "SQL Server," "database," and "trend analysis" more prominent and consistent.
5. In the current Corvane entry, consider revising the Python bullet to foreground data-processing and validation terminology without overstating scale: "Developed Python data-processing tools using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to ingest rig output files, validate every channel against test specifications, and generate standard report figures; reduced report preparation time from about three days to half a day per test." Use this only as a clearer description of the work already documented.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
